instruction: Change request for the A0 front end (lexer and parser): withdraw the accepted spellings `udiv` and `urem`; only `div` and `rem` name those operations now. A node `a udiv p0 p1` then reads `udiv` as the name of a function it calls, which is a structure error when no earlier function has that name. The parser reports the first diagnostic as (code, token index), code 1 a parse error and 2 a structure error; token indexes count the tokens of the lexer (comments and spaces make no tokens; each newline is one).

tests.src:
fn f u32 u32 -> u32
a udiv p0 p1
ret a
end

fn f u32 u32 -> u32
a div p0 p1
ret urem a p1
end

fn urem u32 u32 -> u32
ret p0
end
fn g u32 -> u32
a urem p0 2
b rem a 2
ret b
end

fn sq u32 -> u32
a mul p0 p0
ret a
end

# a small program
use "lib.a0"
fn inc u32 -> u32
a add p0 1 # one more

end
fn g u32x4 (u32,bool) -> u32
b at p1 0
c get p0 2
d call inc c
e div d 3
f select true e b
t text "hi\n"
ret f
end

fn h u32x4x2 boolx3 -> (u32,u32x4)
x get p0 1
y get x 0
z rec y x
ret z
end
fn k u32 u32 -> u32
ret sub p0 p1
end

wrong.why: both: only `udiv` is withdrawn, `urem` is still read as `rem`
